{{Short description|Swedish jazz trumpeter and composer (born 1934)}}
{{more footnotes|date=January 2015}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=December 2020}}

'''Jan Bertil Allan''' (born 7 November 1934)<ref name=":0" /> is a [[Sweden|Swedish]] [[jazz]] trumpeter and composer.<ref name="RCJE">{{Cite book
 | last = Cook
 | first = Richard
 | year = 2005
 | title = Richard Cook's Jazz Encyclopedia
 | publisher = Penguin Books
 | location = London
 | isbn = 0-141-00646-3
 | pages = 8
}}</ref> He is the winner of a [[Grammis]] Award, the Swedish equivalent of the [[Grammys]].<ref name="grammis"/> He has also composed for several films such as ''[[The Adventures of Picasso]]'' (1978), ''[[Sopor (film)|Sopor]]'' (1981) and ''[[Trollkarlen (film)|Trollkarlen]]'' (1999).

==Career==
Allan was born 7 November 1934 in [[Falun, Sweden]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |url=http://193.10.144.138/sv/svensk-film/Filmdatabasen/?type=PERSON&itemid=71865 |title=Svenska Filminstitutet |access-date=28 January 2010 |archive-date=10 August 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160810021246/http://193.10.144.138/sv/svensk-film/Filmdatabasen/?type=PERSON&itemid=71865 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He began his career in 1951 as a pianist; after moving to [[Stockholm]], he changed to the trumpet as his main instrument. At this time he played in [[Carl-Henrik Norin]]'s orchestra. From 1954 to 1955, he worked with [[Lars Gullin]] and [[Rolf Billberg]] and from 1955 to 1959 with Carl-Henrik Norin. At the same time, he earned a [[PhD]] in [[physics]].

Despite his small number of records, Allan is among the most important modern [[jazz]] musicians in Sweden. From 1960 to 1963, he led a quintet with Billberg. Over the course of the 1960s, he worked with [[Arne Domnérus]], [[Georg Riedel (jazz musician)|Georg Riedel]], and [[Bengt Hallberg]], among others. From 1968 to 1975, he was a member of the [[Swedish Radio Jazz Group]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=A Swedish jazz legend - Berwaldhallen|url=https://www.berwaldhallen.se/en/concert/a-swedish-jazz-legend/|access-date=2020-10-01|website=www.berwaldhallen.se|language=en}}</ref> His album ''Jan Allan -70'', which featured [[Rolf Ericson]], [[Nils Lindberg]], [[Bobo Stenson]], [[Jon Christensen (musician)|Jon Christensen]], and [[Rune Gustafsson]], won a Grammis Award for Jazz of the Year in 1970.<ref name="grammis">[http://grammis.se/nominerade/1970/ 1970 Grammis Award nominees and winners] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150128113854/http://grammis.se/nominerade/1970/ |date=28 January 2015 }} (Swedish)</ref> Allan played with the same group and Georg Riedel on the trio-album ''Sweet And Loverly''. His 1998 album ''Software'' stands in strong affinity with the [[West Coast Jazz]] of [[Gerry Mulligan]] and [[Stan Getz]].

Over the course of his career, Allan recorded albums with [[Bosse Broberg]], [[Benny Carter]], [[Dorothy Donegan]], [[Lars Gullin]], [[Jan Johansson (jazz musician)|Jan Johansson]], [[Thad Jones]], [[Roger Kellaway]], [[Lee Konitz]], [[Nils Lindberg]], [[Georg Riedel (jazz musician)|Georg Riedel]], [[George Russell (composer)|George Russell]] and [[Monica Zetterlund]]. In 2009, he was honored with a Swedish [[Golden Django]] as a Master of Jazz.

In 2000, his Bach trumpet, which was engraved with his name and he played for 35 years, was stolen.<ref>{{Cite web|last=oj-admin|date=2012-02-10|title=Håll koll efter Jan Allans trumpet!|url=https://orkesterjournalen.com/wordpress/?p=3688|access-date=2020-10-01|website=OrkesterJournalen|language=sv-SE}}{{Dead link|date=January 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> A movie about the theft and missing trumpet was broadcast on Swedish television in 2015; it had an audience of 1.1 million viewers.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sannsagan om en stulen trumpet Tom Alandh har gjort en film inspirerad av nedanstående historia. Dokumentären "Jan Allan och trumpeten som försvann" sändes i SVT1 den 4/1 2015 och hade 1.1 miljoner tittare. Sprid denna historia! Uppmana alla du känner att läsa och hålla ögonen öppna. Sprid det på nätet och på krogen. Berätta för musikanter, för pantbanker, försäljare ... och uppmana till att vara noga med att om möjligt kontrollera ett objekts ursprung, innan man köper det. För samtliga bestulnas skull. "I ett perspektiv, bara en bit metall ... I ett annat perspektiv, en av de mest betydelsefulla instrumenten i svensk musikhistoria." Citat trumpetaren Peter Asplund|url=https://www.annallan.se/Ann_Allans_hemsida/Anns_blogg/Poster/2012/2/9.html|access-date=2020-10-01|website=www.annallan.se|archive-date=16 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210516221930/https://www.annallan.se/Ann_Allans_hemsida/Anns_blogg/Poster/2012/2/9.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>
